summary: Today’s pulse tracks Burnham to review early prisoner release scheme amid anger over potential freeing of PC Harper’s killers – UK politics live, New Ukraine army chief vows to step up counteroffensive as EU bids to finalise fresh Russia sanctions – Europe live, and Salman Rushdie attacker faces US terrorism trial. Across Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are burnham, defence, and europe. In the background, Burnham announces £2 bus fare cap across England from January and Venezuela’s Maduro in court for pre-trial hearing in US drug trafficking case keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Burnham to review early prisoner release scheme amid anger over potential freeing of PC Harper’s killers – UK politics live
headlines.description: New PM says the main perpetrator in the killing of PC Andrew Harper will now ‘not be subject to early release’ and he will also review ‘whole policy’ Wes Streeting said the US president was “right” to demand Europe pays more for its own defence. Donald Trump has been increasingly critical of Europe for relying too much on the US for its security, and has demanded Nato allies reach 5% of GDP on defence spending by 2035. President Trump has called on Europe to carry a greater share of the burden for our own defence, and he is right to do so. The UK has always been a leading light on defence spending, but the world is changing and in these dangerous uncertain times it is clear that we have needed to go further. That’s why we’ve committed £298bn over the next four years, including an additional £15bn on top of last year’s spending review settlement. At the recent Nato summit, all members reaffirmed our commitment to 3.5 by 35 [3.5% of GDP by 2035].

headlines.title: New Ukraine army chief vows to step up counteroffensive as EU bids to finalise fresh Russia sanctions – Europe live
headlines.description: Brussels talks between senior diplomats now underway in attempt to sign off 21st package of sanctions, after previous failed attempts The Venice Biennale said it would challenge a European Union decision to withdraw a €2 ⁠million grant in response to the return of Russia to its 2026 edition, despite continuing aggression on Ukraine, Reuters reported. The Italian government sharply criticised the move, while the European Commission warned it ​would suspend or terminate funding if the Russian ‌pavilion returned.

headlines.title: Salman Rushdie attacker faces US terrorism trial
headlines.description: Hadi Matar, already serving 25 years for attempted murder, denies federal charges that could bring a life sentence The man who stabbed Salman Rushdie in the eye on stage in 2022 is standing trial for a second time – this time facing terrorism charges after being found guilty of attempted murder and sentenced to 25 years in prison last year. Hadi Matar’s federal trial begins in Buffalo, New York on Wednesday, about 70 miles from the venue where Rushdie was due to speak about writers in political exile in August 2022, when he was stabbed more than a dozen times.

headlines.title: Burnham announces £2 bus fare cap across England from January
headlines.description: Measure to cost more than £500m, with money allocated to allow devolved nations to do the same UK politics live – latest updates Single bus fares across England will be capped at £2 from January, Andy Burnham has announced, as he continues to introduce measures to tackle the cost of living in his first week as prime minister. The nationwide cap is currently set at £3 until the end of March 2027, although some areas – including London and Greater Manchester, where Burnham set a £2 limit as mayor – have lower top rates for single tickets.

headlines.title: Venezuela’s Maduro in court for pre-trial hearing in US drug trafficking case
headlines.description: Venezuelan president and his wife, Cilia Flores, have been held at Brooklyn jail and both have pleaded not guilty Nicolás Maduro returns to court with his lawyers Wednesday and is expected to continue objecting to the US military action that snatched the Venezuelan president from power and deposited him in New York to face drug trafficking charges. Maduro, 63, and his wife Cilia Flores, 69, have been held at a Brooklyn jail ever since US forces seized them from their Caracas home in a stunning middle-of-the-night raid and brought them to New York in early January.

headlines.title: US teen buys Wilt Chamberlain jacket in thrift store that sells for $89,600
headlines.description: The $3 purchase was authenticated as a rare piece from Chamberlain’s final NBA season An Oregon teenager admitted “I got very, very lucky” after a basketball legend’s jacket he picked up at a thrift store for pocket change sold at auction for almost $90,000. Quinn Brown said he was in a Goodwill store in Portland in January when he saw somebody throw the bright yellow jacket into a clothing bin.

headlinePool.title: Trump ally pledges to ‘work with people’ he disagrees with after Arizona primary win – US politics live
headlinePool.description: Andy Biggs – a hard-right congressman endorsed by Donald Trump – won the Republican nomination for Arizona governor Donald Trump took to Truth Social a short while and noted that the US will destroy one bridge or power plant , including those near Tehran, “any time” that Iran “shoots a ship” in the strait of Hormuz.

headlinePool.title: Fifth person dies in New York City amid legionnaires’ disease outbreak
headlinePool.description: Outbreak has been traced to Upper East Side cooling towers, but Mamdani says source of exposure has been eliminated A fifth person has died in New York City in connection with the legionnaires’ disease outbreak on Manhattan’s Upper East Side neighborhood, according to the city’s health department. In an update issued Tuesday, the department said that 82 cases of legionnaires’ disease have now been identified and five people have died. Eight people remain hospitalized, while 56 have been discharged.

headlinePool.title: Europe’s heatwave in June cost grain farmers €2bn in lost revenue and crop damage
headlinePool.description: EU set for worst crop harvest in decade after total grain yield estimated to be 9m tonnes smaller than expected, analysis finds The heatwave that swept across Europe in June is estimated to have cost the continent’s grain farmers €2bn (£1.7bn) in lost revenue and destroyed 10m tonnes of crops, according to a new analysis, raising concern about the impact on food prices. The European harvest of crops including wheat, barley, maize and oats is now predicted to be 9m tonnes smaller than forecast before the June heatwave, according to Coceral, the European association which represents trade of cereals and oilseeds.

headlinePool.title: Bus fare cap coming from aid budget will hit world’s poorest, Burnham told
headlinePool.description: Funding proposal for cost of living policy ‘throws global south countries under the bus’, says ActionAid UK director Burnham announces bus fares to be capped at £2 UK politics live – latest updates The world’s most vulnerable people will be put at risk by Andy Burnham’s decision to use the aid budget to pay for cheaper bus fares in England, charities have said. The prime minister announced on Wednesday that he would reduce the fare cap from £3 per journey to £2 for next year, funded mainly by changing international climate donations into repayable loans.

headlinePool.title: Trump threatens to destroy Iranian bridges and power plants in retaliation for strait of Hormuz attacks – Middle East crisis live
headlinePool.description: Threat from US president comes after US military completes 11th night of strikes on Iran The Jordanian army said it intercepted four Iranian missiles on Wednesday with two additional missile falling in an open area, AFP reports. The two missiles that the army did not intercept fell in “two remote, uninhabited areas, without causing any human casualties or material damage” the army said in a statement.

headlinePool.title: Greetings from Jerusalem, whose holy sites host some of the oldest colonies of nesting swifts
headlinePool.description: The scythe-winged birds have nested in the cracks of the Western Wall and other holy sites in Jerusalem for thousands of years.

headlinePool.title: Model scout for Jeffrey Epstein found dead at his home near Paris
headlinePool.description: Daniel Siad faced allegations of rape and trafficking in France and appeared in more than 1,000 documents in Epstein files A modelling scout who recruited women for Jeffrey Epstein has been found dead at his home near Paris, French officials have said. Daniel Siad, 69, was under investigation by the prosecutors specialising in human trafficking in France, accused of rape and other charges. His name appeared in more than 1,000 documents in the US Department of Justice Epstein files that were declassified earlier this year.

headlinePool.title: Nicaragua’s congress announces ‘work plan’ to suspend elections
headlinePool.description: US secretary of state says international community should ‘join forces’ against authoritarian Ortega regime Nicaragua’s congress, controlled by the country’s long-serving president, Daniel Ortega, has announced a “work plan” to implement the authoritarian leader’s order that the country should no longer hold elections. The UN and the US strongly condemned Sunday’s announcement by Ortega, who has been in power since 2007 and, after a controversial constitutional change last year, now governs alongside his wife, Rosario Murillo, as “co-president”.

headlinePool.title: Harry Potter publisher to receive millions in Anthropic copyright settlement
headlinePool.description: Bloomsbury has 14,087 titles listed within settlement between AI startup and authors over use of protected work The publisher of Harry Potter has received a multimillion-pound payout as a beneficiary of a $1.5bn (£1.12bn) copyright settlement between the AI startup Anthropic and thousands of authors over the use of their protected work to power chatbots. Bloomsbury, which is home to the bestselling novelists Sarah J Maas and Susanna Clarke as well as JK Rowling, said it had 14,087 titles listed within the settlement, with a proposed compensation of about $3,000 a title.
